title: harden-prefetch-handshake-and-header-mapping-for-streaming-toolcalls
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Tighten streaming preflight auth handshake, add explicit header mapping for OpenAI-compat tokens, and introduce an ephemeral nonce signature header for long-lived SSE/websocket streams. Backwards compatible: old Authorization passthrough continues to work for non-streaming endpoints.
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of production instability with streaming tool/function calls in the OpenAI-compat layer: (1) opaque CORS/preflight interactions where upstream proxies strip or rewrite special auth headers leading to silent auth failures during long-lived connections, and (2) ambiguous token semantics across org vs project keys that made routing and rate-limits inaccurate for deduped sessions. This PR introduces a conservative, backwards-compatible handshake and a small header schema to make streaming preflight and tool call signing explicit and more robust.

What this PR does (single string with checklist):
- Introduces an explicit prefetch handshake header X-RW-PREFETCH that servers may echo during preflight to indicate which downstream headers must be preserved by proxies (x-rw-scope, x-rw-nonce, x-rw-nonce-sig). 
- Adds a compact scope hint header X-RW-SCOPE with values "org:<org-id>" or "proj:<proj-id>" so downstream routers can keep tenant affinity even when Authorization is stripped for telemetry reasons.
- Adds ephemeral streaming nonce (X-RW-NONCE) and signature (X-RW-NONCE-SIG) headers for SSE/WebSocket upgrades and chunked-transfer streaming to validate that the handshake was performed by the initiating client. Signature format: base64(HMAC-SHA256(nonce || path || ts)) where ts is unix seconds included as X-RW-NONCE-TS to make replays harder.
- Mapping layer for OpenAI-compat: Authorization: Bearer sk-... is mapped to internal headers but we now also accept Organization/Project-prefixed tokens and surface them via X-RW-SCOPE instead of relying on opaque Authorization parsing alone. This reduces routing ambiguity for shared infra.
- Updated CORS allowed headers and preflight responses to explicitly expose the new headers and the ability to echo X-RW-PREFETCH.
- Small SDK surface updates (TS + Python): automatic preflight header injection for browser SDKs and a helper to produce the nonce/signature pair for long-lived streams.
- Tests: unit tests for header parsing, integration test that asserts correct preflight response across a simulated proxy that strips Authorization.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default behavior: if X-RW-PREFETCH is not present, current behavior is unchanged. The header is additive and can be enabled incrementally by customers via route-level config in the Console.
- We ship the server-side acceptors behind a feature flag for two weeks and flip the flag cluster-wide after monitoring the rollout metrics (ENG-1842).
- SDKs include a no-op if the server doesn't advertise X-RW-PREFETCH.

Security considerations:
- Nonce signature uses a per-instance service key; we validated key rotation semantics in the keymanager changeset. Replays are mitigated via X-RW-NONCE-TS and a 30s validity window.
- Reviewed with security (Arjun) and fixed a headroom issue where long Authorization headers could be truncated by proxies if mapped inline; we now send the minimum derived headers instead of passing entire token.

Testing and CI notes:
- All unit and integration tests added to runtime/auth and openai-compat were green after fixups. There was a transient flaky SSE test on linux-arm which required a small timing tolerance bump.

What I would like reviewed:
- Naming of X-RW-PREFETCH / X-RW-SCOPE (Sofia requested a short discussion in code review about alternate names),
- Nonce lifetime and tolerance knobs (Daniel requested explicit config),
- SDK ergonomics for browser preflight injection.

Related: SUP-412 incident postmortem referenced flaky proxy header behavior, and ENG-1899 tracks the metrics dashboard for stray 401s during stream upgrades.
